commands.help:
Rewrite TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, C, C++, Go, Ruby, Java or Kotlin apps in Mojo, one verified piece at a time

Usage: mojo-anything <COMMAND>

Commands:
  analyze  1. Map a repository and write a ranked, ordered migration plan
  bridge   2. Scaffold the port of one unit, with the bindings its callers need
  refresh  2b. Regenerate the bindings from the signatures in the port (`port.mojo`)
  record   3a. Record what the original's functions return on generated and given inputs
  build    3b. Build the port (Node-API addon, Python extension, shared library)
  diff     3c. Replay recorded cases against the built Mojo port
  bench    3d. Time the recorded cases on the original and on the Mojo port, bridge included
  fuzz     3e. Run fresh inputs from a new seed through the original and the port and report where they differ: what the recorded cases did not cover
  profile  Run a real workload under the language's profiler and say what to port: hot functions, their callers, and loops to batch. `mojo-anything profile <repo> -- node bench.mjs` (also `python3 x.py`, `go test -bench . ./pkg`, `java ...`, `ruby x.rb`)
  shadow   4. Generate a drop-in module that runs the original and the Mojo port side by side
  gate     5. Check the definition of done for a port
  package  6. Lay out installable packages and a CI workflow for every platform; never publishes
  app      Record the whole app's behavior and replay any build against it (CLIs)
  mcp      Serve every step as MCP tools over stdio
  setup    Register mojo-anything with your coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode): the MCP server and, where the agent reads skills, the workflow skill. Keeps your other settings; run it again any time
  map      Map the port: every unit of the original, the Mojo port of it, its cases and last diff, the whole app's glue, and which recordings the original changed past since they were made. Commit the map (`--write`) to see upstream changes in it
  doctor   Check pixi and the pinned Mojo, the language runtimes, the agent setup and the MCP server, with the command that fixes each problem. Exits 1 when something required is missing
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

Loop per unit: analyze -> bridge -> record -> port port.mojo -> build -> diff -> shadow -> gate

1. Map a repository and write a ranked, ordered migration plan

Usage: mojo-anything analyze [OPTIONS] [ROOT]

Arguments:
  [ROOT]  Repository root [default: .]

Options:
      --json         Print the machine-readable report (schema `mojo-anything/analyze@1`) instead of Markdown
  -o, --out <OUT>    Write to this file instead of stdout
      --lang <LANG>  Source language; detected from the repository when omitted [possible values: ts, python, c, go, ruby, java, kotlin, php, csharp, cpp]
      --whole-app    Plan a whole-app port: entry points and shape, every dependency (imported or declared) with its Mojo replacement, pieces in port order, and decisions for the user
  -h, --help         Print help

2. Scaffold the port of one unit, with the bindings its callers need

Usage: mojo-anything bridge [OPTIONS] <ROOT> <UNIT>

Arguments:
  <ROOT>
          Repository root

  <UNIT>
          Unit id, as `analyze` lists it

Options:
      --kind <KIND>
          Bridge to generate; defaults to the plan's choice

          Possible values:
          - node: A Mojo port behind a Node-API addon
          - wasm: A Mojo port compiled to a WebAssembly module (wasm64), loaded by `index.cjs`

  -o, --out <OUT>
          Port folder; defaults to `<root>/mojo/<name>`

      --name <NAME>
          Port name; defaults to `<unit>-mojo`

      --force
          Bridge a unit the plan marks blocked or keep

      --keep <KEEP>
          Keep an export in TS: `name` or `"name: reason"`. Repeatable

      --batch <BATCH>
          Add a batch class: `function:param` runs `function` over many `param` values kept on the native side (what `profile` recommends for leaves called in loops)

      --as-json <TYPE_PARAM>
          Bridge a type parameter as JSON values (`--as-json T`) when the app only fills it with data, instead of keeping the generic export in TS. Repeatable

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

2b. Regenerate the bindings from the signatures in the port (`port.mojo`)

Usage: mojo-anything refresh [OPTIONS] [PORT_DIR]

Arguments:
  [PORT_DIR]  [default: .]

Options:
      --batch <BATCH>  Add a batch class: `function:param` runs `function` over many `param` values kept on the native side. Repeat for more
  -h, --help           Print help

3a. Record what the original's functions return on generated and given inputs

Usage: mojo-anything record [OPTIONS] [PORT_DIR] [-- <TEST_COMMAND>...]

Arguments:
  [PORT_DIR]
          Port folder made by `bridge`
          
          [default: .]

  [TEST_COMMAND]...
          The test command for `--from-tests`, after `--`; it runs in the original's folder

Options:
      --count <COUNT>
          Generated cases per function
          
          [default: 200]

      --inputs <INPUTS>
          Extra cases: JSONL of `{"fn": name, "args": [...]}`

      --module <MODULE>
          Import the original from this JS module (e.g. built output) instead of the TS source

      --resolve-from <RESOLVE_FROM>
          Resolve npm packages from this folder's `node_modules` (when the repo has none installed)

      --node-arg <NODE_ARGS>
          Extra arguments for node, e.g. `--node-arg=--import=tsx`

      --float-tolerance <FLOAT_TOLERANCE>
          Floats match when they differ by at most this times the larger magnitude (absolute below 1), e.g. 1e-9 for numeric code. Saved with the port for diff and gate; 0 removes it

      --from-tests
          Also record every call the original's own test suite makes to the unit's functions: `--from-tests -- npx jest` (TS/JS, any runner) or `-- pytest` (Python)

      --profile <PROFILE>
          Target: this machine

          Possible values:
          - host: This machine
          
          [default: host]

      --pin-clock
          Pin the clock and random numbers while recording and diffing (TS/JS with the node bridge, Python): `Date.now()`, `new Date()` and `Math.random` (`time.time`, `datetime.now` and `random`) get fixed values, saved in `pinned.json`, and the port reads them from `pinned.mojo`. Kept for later runs until `--no-pin-clock`

      --no-pin-clock
          Stop pinning the clock and random numbers

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

3b. Build the port (Node-API addon, Python extension, shared library)

Usage: mojo-anything build [OPTIONS] [PORT_DIR]

Arguments:
  [PORT_DIR]
          [default: .]

Options:
      --profile <PROFILE>
          Target: this machine

          Possible values:
          - host: This machine
          
          [default: host]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

3c. Replay recorded cases against the built Mojo port

Usage: mojo-anything diff [OPTIONS] [PORT_DIR]

Arguments:
  [PORT_DIR]
          [default: .]

Options:
      --profile <PROFILE>
          Target: this machine

          Possible values:
          - host: This machine
          
          [default: host]

      --module <MODULE>
          Test this JS module instead of the port's `index.cjs`

      --ignore-key-order
          Compare objects regardless of key order

      --float-tolerance <FLOAT_TOLERANCE>
          Floats match within this tolerance for this run (the one saved by `record` otherwise)

      --json
          

      --node-arg <NODE_ARGS>
          

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

3d. Time the recorded cases on the original and on the Mojo port, bridge included

Usage: mojo-anything bench [OPTIONS] [PORT_DIR]

Arguments:
  [PORT_DIR]  [default: .]

Options:
      --min-ms <MIN_MS>              Minimum measured time per function and side, in milliseconds [default: 200]
      --resolve-from <RESOLVE_FROM>  Resolve npm packages the original imports from this folder's `node_modules`
      --json                         
      --node-arg <NODE_ARGS>         
  -h, --help                         Print help

3e. Run fresh inputs from a new seed through the original and the port and report where they differ: what the recorded cases did not cover

Usage: mojo-anything fuzz [OPTIONS] [PORT_DIR]

Arguments:
  [PORT_DIR]
          [default: .]

Options:
      --cases <CASES>
          Fresh cases per function (and scenarios per class) in each round
          
          [default: 200]

      --seed <SEED>
          Seed of the first round; random (and printed) when omitted. Later rounds count up

      --time <SECS>
          Keep running new rounds until this many seconds have passed (one round otherwise)

      --keep[=<KEEP>]
          Append the mismatching cases (`--keep`) or every fresh case (`--keep=all`) to `cases.jsonl`, so the next diff and gate check them

          Possible values:
          - mismatches: Only the cases where the port differs from the original
          - all:        Every fresh case

      --resolve-from <RESOLVE_FROM>
          Resolve npm packages the original imports from this folder's `node_modules`

      --json
          

      --node-arg <NODE_ARGS>
          

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Run a real workload under the language's profiler and say what to port: hot functions, their callers, and loops to batch. `mojo-anything profile <repo> -- node bench.mjs` (also `python3 x.py`, `go test -bench . ./pkg`, `java ...`, `ruby x.rb`)

Usage: mojo-anything profile [OPTIONS] <ROOT> -- <COMMAND>...

Arguments:
  <ROOT>        Repository root
  <COMMAND>...  The workload, after `--`

Options:
      --json         
      --lang <LANG>  Source language; detected from the repository when omitted [possible values: ts, python, c, go, ruby, java, kotlin, php, csharp, cpp]
  -h, --help         Print help

4. Generate a drop-in module that runs the original and the Mojo port side by side

Usage: mojo-anything shadow [OPTIONS] [PORT_DIR]

Arguments:
  [PORT_DIR]  [default: .]

Options:
  -o, --out <OUT>  Where to write the module; defaults to `<port>/shadow/<name>.shadow.ts`
  -h, --help       Print help

5. Check the definition of done for a port

Usage: mojo-anything gate [OPTIONS] [PORT_DIR]

Arguments:
  [PORT_DIR]  [default: .]

Options:
      --json                  
      --node-arg <NODE_ARGS>  
  -h, --help                  Print help

6. Lay out installable packages and a CI workflow for every platform; never publishes

Usage: mojo-anything package [OPTIONS] [PORT_DIR]

Arguments:
  [PORT_DIR]  [default: .]

Options:
      --name <NAME>        Package name (npm, PyPI, RubyGems, Maven artifact); defaults to the unit's name
      --version <VERSION>  Package version; defaults to the original package's
      --out <OUT>          Output folder; defaults to `<port>/package`
      --dry-run            List the files, write nothing
      --json               
  -h, --help               Print help

Record the whole app's behavior and replay any build against it (CLIs)

Usage: mojo-anything app <COMMAND>

Commands:
  record      Run the original CLI on cases (its own examples, `--inputs`, semantic traps), twice each, and store them as trycmd files in `<repo>/mojo/app-cases/`. `mojo-anything app record . -- python3 cli.py`
  replay      Run a build against `<repo>/mojo/app-cases/`, print passed/total, write a report with a diff per failing case; exits non-zero on any mismatch
  front-door  Scaffold `<repo>/mojo/app`, the Mojo binary that owns the CLI's entry point: it routes the recorded commands and options, every command running the original until a unit is wired. Builds it and replays the cases (every case passes, every case falling back)
  wire        Hand commands to a unit's port (after it passes gate): adds the unit to `mojo/app`, a glue file to write once (a CLI), the routing and a kill switch (`MOJO_ANYTHING_UNIT_<NAME>=original`), then builds and replays. A CLI or a library takes a Mojo unit (`mojo/<name>` with `port.mojo`); a server takes one for each route
  lift        Make `mojo/app` a pure app (a Mojo binary for a CLI), once replay passes with fallback rate 0 and every unit passes gate: removes the fallback and the kill switches, strips the units' bridges, runs the lift checklist and replays the pure binary. Checked on a copy first; the original stays in place
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Run the original CLI on cases (its own examples, `--inputs`, semantic traps), twice each, and store them as trycmd files in `<repo>/mojo/app-cases/`. `mojo-anything app record . -- python3 cli.py`

Usage: mojo-anything app record [OPTIONS] [REPO] [-- <RUN>...]

Arguments:
  [REPO]    Repository root [default: .]
  [RUN]...  The command that runs the original, after `--`; paths are relative to the repository. Taken from the saved cases when omitted

Options:
      --inputs <INPUTS>
          Extra cases: JSONL of `{"name", "args": [...], "stdin", "env": {...}, "files": {path: text}}`
      --normalize <NORMALIZE>
          Normalizer: `timestamps`, `uuids`, `key-order`, or `name=regex` for your own. Repeatable; saved with the cases
      --name <NAME>
          The name the app is invoked by in its docs (found from the command and manifests when omitted)
      --no-traps
          Leave out the semantic-trap inputs
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>
          Seconds before a run is killed (default 30)
      --http
          The app is a server: the command starts it, taking its port from PORT or `{port}`; cases are requests (curl lines in its docs, `--inputs`, traps), kept in `http/`
      --port <PORT>
          A port the server always listens on (implies --http)
      --arg <ARG>
          An argument every server start gets after its command, the original's and every build's (`{port}` is the port each one is given: the front door's public port, and its original's own), so a build is started as the original is (`--arg db.json`). Repeatable; implies --http; saved with the cases
      --fresh <FRESH>
          A file or folder of the repository the app reads or writes (a project tree, a database file, a public folder): snapshotted into `files/` (`http/files/` for a server) and copied into a fresh working directory before every case (CLIs) or start (servers). A CLI's written files are what differs from it afterwards, and the files it removed are compared too. Repeatable; saved with the cases
      --pace <MS>
          Milliseconds to wait after each response before the next request, for work a server does after answering (a file watcher reloading what it just wrote). Implies --http; saved with the cases and used by replay; 0 removes it
      --float-tolerance <FLOAT_TOLERANCE>
          Numbers in the output match when they differ by at most this times the larger magnitude (absolute below 1), e.g. 1e-9 for numeric code. Saved with the cases; 0 removes it
      --float-file <PATH=FORMAT>
          A written file of raw floats, compared value by value within --float-tolerance instead of byte for byte: `PATH=f32le` or `PATH=f64le`. Repeatable; saved with the cases
      --effects <KINDS>
          Record what leaves the process too: `http` runs a local sink that answers every request (set as HTTP_PROXY, http_proxy and MOJO_ANYTHING_HTTP_SINK), `smtp` a local mail server (SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT). Each case stores what reached them, in order, and replay compares it. Comma-separated or repeated. Saved with the cases
      --effect-env <VAR=KIND>
          Point one of the app's own settings at a sink: VAR=http-url, VAR=smtp-host, VAR=smtp-port or VAR=smtp-url (e.g. WEBHOOK_URL=http-url). Implies that effect
      --db-reset <COMMAND>
          A shell command run before each case (CLIs) or each start (servers) that resets the database to a known state. Cases then run one at a time
      --db-dump <COMMAND>
          A shell command that prints the database's state (e.g. `sqlite3 app.db .dump`), run after each case or request; its output is recorded with the effects
      --json
          
  -h, --help
          Print help

Run a build against `<repo>/mojo/app-cases/`, print passed/total, write a report with a diff per failing case; exits non-zero on any mismatch

Usage: mojo-anything app replay [OPTIONS] [REPO]

Arguments:
  [REPO]  Repository root [default: .]

Options:
      --build <BUILD>      Command line of the build to test (the original, the front door, the final binary); the original when omitted
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>  Seconds before a run is killed
      --port <PORT>        Servers: the port the build always listens on; otherwise it gets a free one through PORT and `{port}`
      --case <CASE>        Replay only this case, by the name the report gives it (a library: only this unit). The fast, repeatable loop for fixing one mismatch
      --json               
  -h, --help               Print help

Scaffold `<repo>/mojo/app`, the Mojo binary that owns the CLI's entry point: it routes the recorded commands and options, every command running the original until a unit is wired. Builds it and replays the cases (every case passes, every case falling back)

Usage: mojo-anything app front-door [OPTIONS] [REPO]

Arguments:
  [REPO]  Repository root [default: .]

Options:
      --no-check  Only write the files; skip the build and replay
      --library   Treat the repository as a library even if it has a `main`: the front door is a Mojo package with the public API (found by default when there is no main and no server)
      --json      
  -h, --help      Print help

Hand commands to a unit's port (after it passes gate): adds the unit to `mojo/app`, a glue file to write once (a CLI), the routing and a kill switch (`MOJO_ANYTHING_UNIT_<NAME>=original`), then builds and replays. A CLI or a library takes a Mojo unit (`mojo/<name>` with `port.mojo`); a server takes one for each route

Usage: mojo-anything app wire [OPTIONS] <REPO> <UNIT>

Arguments:
  <REPO>  Repository root
  <UNIT>  The unit: its folder, its name under `mojo/`, or the unit id it was bridged from

Options:
      --command <COMMANDS>  A command the unit answers. Repeatable; kept from the last wire when omitted
      --route <ROUTES>      Servers: a route the unit answers (`GET /users/{id}`, `/files/{*rest}`, `/path` for any method, `*` for everything else). Repeatable; kept from the last wire when omitted
      --skip-gate           Do not run gate on the unit first (it just passed)
      --no-check            Only write the files; skip the build and replay
      --json                
  -h, --help                Print help

Make `mojo/app` a pure app (a Mojo binary for a CLI), once replay passes with fallback rate 0 and every unit passes gate: removes the fallback and the kill switches, strips the units' bridges, runs the lift checklist and replays the pure binary. Checked on a copy first; the original stays in place

Usage: mojo-anything app lift [OPTIONS] [REPO]

Arguments:
  [REPO]  Repository root [default: .]

Options:
      --json  
  -h, --help  Print help

Serve every step as MCP tools over stdio

Usage: mojo-anything mcp

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Register mojo-anything with your coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode): the MCP server and, where the agent reads skills, the workflow skill. Keeps your other settings; run it again any time

Usage: mojo-anything setup [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --agent <AGENTS>
          Agents to set up (repeatable); every agent found by default

          Possible values:
          - claude:   Claude Code: `~/.claude.json`, skill in `~/.claude/skills`
          - codex:    OpenAI Codex CLI: `~/.codex/config.toml`, skill in `~/.codex/skills`
          - cursor:   Cursor: `~/.cursor/mcp.json`
          - gemini:   Gemini CLI: `~/.gemini/settings.json`
          - opencode: OpenCode: `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, skill in `~/.config/opencode/skills`

      --remove
          Take the mojo-anything entries out again

      --dry-run
          Show what would change, write nothing

      --no-backup
          Change settings files in place without saving a `.mojo-anything.bak` copy first

      --json
          

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Map the port: every unit of the original, the Mojo port of it, its cases and last diff, the whole app's glue, and which recordings the original changed past since they were made. Commit the map (`--write`) to see upstream changes in it

Usage: mojo-anything map [OPTIONS] [REPO]

Arguments:
  [REPO]  Repository root [default: .]

Options:
      --crates <DIR>  Also look for ports in this folder (ports kept outside the repository)
      --write         Write the map to mojo/PORT_MAP.md in the repository instead of printing it
      --check         Exit 1 when the original changed since any port was recorded
      --json          
  -h, --help          Print help

Check pixi and the pinned Mojo, the language runtimes, the agent setup and the MCP server, with the command that fixes each problem. Exits 1 when something required is missing

Usage: mojo-anything doctor [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json  
  -h, --help  Print help
